claim: Vanishing white matter disease (VWM) is a severe leukodystrophy of the central nervous system caused by mutations in subunits of the eukaryotic initiation factor 2B complex (eIF2B).
source: Vanishing white matter disease (VWM) is a severe leukodystrophy of the central nervous system caused by mutations in subunits of the eukaryotic initiation factor 2B complex (eIF2B).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the literature about VWM disease, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Current models only partially recapitulate key disease features of VWM, and pathophysiology is poorly understood.
source: Current models only partially recapitulate key disease features, and pathophysiology is poorly understood.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing mouse models in the introduction (Geva et al., 2010; Dooves et al., 2016).

claim: Zebrafish eif2b mutants phenocopy VWM, including impaired somatic growth, early lethality, effects on myelination, loss of oligodendrocyte precursor cells, increased apoptosis in the CNS, and impaired motor swimming behavior.
source: Through development and validation of zebrafish (Danio rerio) models of VWM, we demonstrate that zebrafish eif2b mutants phenocopy VWM, including impaired somatic growth, early lethality, effects on myelination, loss of oligodendrocyte precursor cells, increased apoptosis in the CNS, and impaired motor swimming behavior.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript, including survival curves, motor behavior analysis, TUNEL staining, and OPC counts.

claim: Expression of human EIF2B2 in the zebrafish eif2b2 mutant rescues lethality and CNS apoptosis.
source: Expression of human EIF2B2 in the zebrafish eif2b2 mutant rescues lethality and CNS apoptosis, demonstrating conservation of function between zebrafish and human.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing survival and TUNEL counts in transgenic rescue experiments (Figure 7).

claim: In the eif2b mutants, intron 12 retention leads to expression of a truncated eif2b5 transcript.
source: In the mutants, intron 12 retention leads to expression of a truncated eif2b5 transcript.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data showing increased intron 12 retention in mutants (Figure 8B).

claim: Expression of the truncated eif2b5 in wild-type larva impairs motor behavior and activates the ISR.
source: Expression of the truncated eif2b5 in wild-type larva impairs motor behavior and activates the ISR, suggesting that a feed-forward mechanism in VWM is a significant component of disease pathophysiology.
evidence: This is supported by motor behavior analysis and qRT-PCR of ISR markers following injection of truncated eif2b5 (Figure 8D, F).

claim: Each human EIF2B subunit gene has a single zebrafish ortholog with a conserved amino acid sequence.
source: Each human EIF2B subunit gene has a single zebrafish ortholog with a conserved amino acid sequence (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The Eif2b zebrafish and human protein structures show conserved structural domains.
source: The Eif2b zebrafish and human protein structures also show conserved structural domains (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by protein domain comparison shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Expression analysis of zebrafish eif2b genes at 24 hpf showed expression chiefly in the brain and eye.
source: Expression analysis of zebrafish eif2b genes at 24 hpf (hours post-fertilization) showed expression chiefly in the brain and eye (Figure 1C–G).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization images shown in Figure 1C-G.

claim: By 72 hpf expression was clearly noted throughout the animal, with higher levels in the brain.
source: By 72 hpf expression was clearly noted throughout the animal, with higher levels in the brain (Figure 1H–L).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization images shown in Figure 1H-L.

claim: Only for eif2b4 were the expression changes significant during the first 7 days of life.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR analysis revealed subunit specific expression changes in the first 7 days of life, although only for eif2b4 were the changes significant (Figure 1M–Q).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1M-Q.

claim: eif2b1 (sa12357) harbors a T/A transversion resulting in an early stop in exon 8.
source: eif2b1 (sa12357) harbors a T/A transversion resulting in an early stop in exon 8 (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is a description of the mutation generated, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: eif2b2 (sa17223) has a G/A transition in exon 5, mutating an essential splice site.
source: eif2b2 (sa17223) has a G/A transition in exon 5, mutating an essential splice site (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is a description of the mutation obtained, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: eif2b4 (sa17367) has a G/A transition in exon 12 mutating an essential splice site.
source: eif2b4 (sa17367) has a G/A transition in exon 12 mutating an essential splice site (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a description of the mutation obtained, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Six different eif2b5 alleles were created by targeting exon 1 using CRISPR/Cas9.
source: To mutagenize subunit eif2b5, we used the Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)/Cas9 system and created six different alleles by targeting exon 1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a description of the mutagenesis approach, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants showed a decrease in size compared to their wild type and heterozygous siblings (2.2 cm vs 1.8 cm, 0.3 and 0.2 s.D., and p<0.0001).
source: The eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants showed a decrease in size compared to their wild type and heterozygous siblings (2.2 cm vs 1.8 cm, 0.3 and 0.2 s.D., and p<0.0001) (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is supported by measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: Mutants of eif2b5zc102/zc102 exhibited growth deficits such as failure to develop a swim bladder, and were smaller in size compared to their wild type and heterozygous siblings.
source: Mutants of a more severe allele, eif2b5zc102/zc102, harboring an early stop codon, exhibited growth deficits such as failure to develop a swim bladder, and were smaller in size compared to their wild type and heterozygous siblings (Figure 2H, arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by brightfield images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 allele exhibited failure to develop a swim bladder.
source: This phenotype was also present in the eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 allele (Figure 2H, arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by brightfield images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Two alleles did not survive past 2 weeks of age: eif2b5zc102/zc102 and eif2b2sa17223/sa17223.
source: Two alleles did not survive past 2 weeks of age: eif2b5zc102/zc102 and eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 (at 10 dpf, eif2b5+/+ WT n = 12; eif2b5zc102/+ heterozygous n = 26; eif2b5zc102/zc102 homozygous n = 0. eif2b2+/+ WT n = 68; eif2b2sa17223/+ heterozygous n = 118; eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 homozygous n = 2) (Figure 2I–J).
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curves shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: The milder phenotype eif2b5zc103 allele survives until adulthood.
source: By contrast, the milder phenotype eif2b5zc103 allele survives until adulthood (at 10 dpf, eif2b5+/+ WT n = 25; eif2b5zc103/+ heterozygous n = 41; eif2b5zc103/zc103 homozygous n = 22) (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curves shown in Figure 2K.

claim: The eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 homozygous mutants showed reduction in distance moved, movement time, and velocity at 7dpf.
source: The eif2b2sa17222sa172232 homozygous mutants showed reduction in distance moved, movement time, and velocity at 7dpf (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is supported by motor behavior analysis shown in Figure 2L.

claim: The eif2b5 zc102/zc102 mutants had motor function impairments by 5 dpf.
source: The eif2b5 zc102/zc102 mutants had motor function impairments by 5 dpf (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is supported by motor behavior analysis shown in Figure 2L.

claim: The eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants had no difference in distance moved, movement time, or velocity as compared to their wild-type siblings.
source: On the other hand, the eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants had no difference in distance moved, movement time, or velocity as compared to their wild-type siblings (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is supported by motor behavior analysis shown in Figure 2L.

claim: At 5 dpf, all three mutant alleles (eif2b5zc103, eif2b5zc102, and eif2b2sa17223) showed an increase in cell death, quantified using TUNEL.
source: At 5 dpf, all three of these mutants showed an increase in cell death, quantified using terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) (eif2b5zc103: mean = 129.1, S.D. = 79.5, eif2b5+/+: mean = 12.2, S.D. = 9.8, p=0.001; eif2b5zc102: mean = 163.7, S.D. = 78.2 eif2b5+/+: mean = 18.7, S.D. = 10.6 p=2.03×10−5; eif2b2sa17223: mean = 202.8, S.D. = 60.8: eif2B2+/+: mean = 37.4, S.D. = 25.2, p=0.0005) (Figure 3A–E).
evidence: This is supported by TUNEL staining and quantification shown in Figure 3A-E.

claim: eif2b5zc103 and eif2b5zc102 mutants showed no change in pH3 cell counts at 5 dpf compared to controls, but showed a noticeable change in proliferation pattern.
source: eif2b5zc103 and eif2b5zc102 mutants showed no change in pH3 cell counts at 5 dpf compared to controls, but showed a noticeable change in proliferation pattern: a lack of proliferation in the outer perimeter of the eyes (arrow) and the tectum (arrowhead), but increased proliferation in the ventricular region (asterisk) (eif2b5zc103: mean = 247.2, S.D. = 44.5, eif2b5+/+: mean = 273.1, S.D. = 43.8, p=0.206; eif2b5zc102: mean = 243.3, S.D. = 40.0, eif2b5+/+: mean = 288.3, S.D. = 32.0, p=0.0238) (Figure 3F–H,J).
evidence: This is supported by pH3 staining and quantification shown in Figure 3F-H, J.

claim: eif2b2sa17223 mutants showed a decrease in pH3 cell counts at 5 dpf compared to controls as well as a change in proliferation pattern.
source: eif2b2sa17223 mutants showed a decrease in pH3 cell counts at 5 dpf compared to controls as well as a change in proliferation pattern (eif2b2sa17223: mean = 185.3, S.D. = 37.8: eif2b2+/+: mean = 271.6, S.D. = 46.7, p=0.0004) (Figure 3I,J).
evidence: This is supported by pH3 staining and quantification shown in Figure 3I, J.

claim: No change in the number of OPCs was observed in the spinal cord of eif2b5zc103, eif2b5zc102, or eif2b2sa17223 mutants.
source: We observed no change in the number of OPCs (measured in two somites directly above the caudal end of the yolk) (eif2b5zc103: mean = 26.6, S.D. = 7.55, eif2b5+/+: mean = 30.71, S.D.=,5.88 p=0.278; eif2b5zc102: mean = 30.6, S.D. = 11.0, eif2b5+/+: mean = 36.6, S.D. = 9.63, p=0.514; eif2b2sa17223: mean = 35.8, S.D. = 5.36, eif2b2+/+: mean = 39.2, S.D. = 4.66, p=0.163) (Figure 3K–O).
evidence: This is supported by Olig2dsRed staining and quantification shown in Figure 3K-O.

claim: All three mutant lines (eif2b5zc103, eif2b5zc102, and eif2b2sa17223) showed significant increases in the number of TUNEL-positive OPCs specifically in the hindbrain.
source: All three lines showed significant increases in the number of TUNEL-positive OPCs specifically in the hindbrain (eif2b5zc102: mean = 17.5, S.D. = 3.02, eif2b5+/+: mean = 1, S.D. = 1, p=0.00004; eif2b5zc103: mean = 3, S.D. = 2.26, eif2b5+/+: mean = 0.7, S.D. = 1.06, p=0.0144; eif2b2sa17223: mean = 3.5, S.D. = 1.05, eif2b2+/+: mean = 0.333, S.D. = 0.577, p=0.002) (Figure 3P–T).
evidence: This is supported by co-labeling of Olig2dsRed and TUNEL shown in Figure 3P-T.

claim: The adult eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants showed a decrease in the thickness of the myelin sheath as measured by estimation of the G-ratio.
source: The adult mutants showed a decrease in the thickness of the myelin sheath as measured by estimation of the G-ratio, the perimeter of the axon to the perimeter of the myelin sheath (eif2b5zc103: mean = 0.690, S.D. = 0.076, eif2b5+/+: mean = 0.593, S.D. = 0.085, p=2.18E-22) (Figure 6A–E).
evidence: This is supported by TEM analysis and G-ratio quantification shown in Figure 6A-E.

claim: The adult eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants showed a disorganized pattern of myelinated axons in the optic tectum compared to age-matched wild-type adult controls.
source: The adult mutants showed a disorganized pattern of myelinated axons in the optic tectum compared to age-matched wild-type adult controls (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is supported by Black Gold II staining shown in Figure 6F-G.

claim: MRI of adult eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants showed a decrease in overall brain size compared to adult wild-type controls.
source: We performed magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of adult eif2b5 mutants, and found a decrease in overall brain size in the adult eif2b5zc103/zc103 mutants compared to adult wild-type controls using the skull as a normalization factor to account for the decrease in overall size of the mutants (Figure 6H–J; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by MRI analysis shown in Figure 6H-J and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transgenic mutant eif2b2sa17223/sa17223;Tg(ß-actin:EIF2B2-2A-eGFP) larva developed a swim bladder and the growth deficits were rescued.
source: The transgenic mutant eif2b2sa17223/ sa17223;Tg(ß-actin:EIF2B2-2A-eGFP) larva developed a swim bladder and the growth deficits were rescued (Figure 7F, arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by brightfield images shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The transgenic homozygous mutant eif2b2sa17223/sa17223;Tg(ß-actin:EIF2B2-2A-eGFP) animals showed 21% survival at 10 dpf (e.g. Mendelian ratios).
source: In contrast the transgenic homozygous mutant eif2b2sa17223/ sa17223;Tg(ß-actin:EIF2B2-2A-eGFP) animals showed 21% survival at 10 dpf (e.g. Mendelian ratios) (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by genotype results shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 increase in apoptosis was rescued and apoptosis in the eif2b2sa17223/sa17223;Tg(ß-actin:EIF2B2-2A-eGFP) was significantly reduced.
source: Further, the eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 increase in apoptosis (Figure 7G–H,K) was rescued and apoptosis in the eif2b2sa17223/sa17223;Tg(ß-actin:EIF2B2-2A-eGFP) was significantly reduced (TUNEL counts eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 transgenic: mean = 31.5, S.D. = 12.9; eif2b2sa17223/sa17223 non-transgenic: mean = 84.4, S.D. = 27.63, p=1.89E-05) (Figure 7I–K).
evidence: This is supported by TUNEL staining and quantification shown in Figure 7G-K.

claim: An increase in retention of intron 12 associated with truncated eif2b5 was found in eif2b mutant alleles (eif2b5: zc102 and zc103; eif2b2: sa17223).
source: We found an increase in retention of intron 12 associated with truncated eif2b5 in eif2b mutant alleles (eif2b5: zc102 and zc103; eif2b2: sa17223) (Figure 8B)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Intron 12 retention was observed in peripheral lymphocytes from a human VWM patient.
source: and which was also observed in peripheral lymphocytes from a human VWM patient (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data from a human patient shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Expression of truncated EIF2B5 in wild-type embryos caused impairment of motor behavior.
source: We observed impairment of motor behavior (Figure 8D), suggesting a dominant-negative effect, although we could not exclude that the effect was caused by over-expression.
evidence: This is supported by motor behavior analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis showed atf4, bip, and chop II expression were increased in eif2b2 and eif2b5 homozygous mutants.
source: qRT-PCR analysis showed atf4, bip, and chop II expression were increased, but perk had variable expression in eif2b2 and eif2b5 homozygous mutants (Figure 8E)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: ISR markers including atf4, chop II, bip and perk, were up-regulated in wild-type embryos expressing truncated EIF2B5.
source: qRT-PCR showed that ISR markers including atf4, chop II, bip and perk, were up-regulated (Figure 8F), indicating that truncated EIF2B5 was sufficient to activate the ISR.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: VWM disease is caused by bi-allelic recessive variants in any of the five genes encoding subunits (1-5) of the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex.
source: VWM disease is caused by bi-allelic recessive variants in any of the five genes encoding subunits (1-5) of the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2B) complex.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about VWM disease.

claim: Symptoms of VWM include ataxia, spasticity, seizures, cognitive impairment, and motor problems.
source: Symptoms of VWM include ataxia, spasticity, seizures, cognitive impairment, and motor problems.
evidence: This is a description of clinical symptoms of VWM disease.

claim: There are no sex differences seen in VWM patients, but females can experience ovarian failure.
source: While there are no sex differences seen in VWM patients, females can experience ovarian failure.
evidence: This is a clinical observation about VWM disease.

claim: In VWM patients, autopsies have revealed affected oligodendrocytes and astrocytes, myelin loss, and cystic cavitations of white matter.
source: In patients, autopsies have revealed affected oligodendrocytes and astrocytes, myelin loss, and cystic cavitations of white matter (van der Knaap et al., 1997; van der Knaap et al., 1998; Pronk et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to autopsy studies.

claim: Genotype-phenotype correlations of mutation severity have been shown in VWM.
source: Genotype-phenotype correlations of mutation severity have been shown (VWM Research Group et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on genotype-phenotype correlations.

claim: Severe multi-organ involvement is characteristic of fetal and neonatal forms of VWM.
source: and severe multi-organ involvement is characteristic of fetal and neonatal forms (van der Knaap et al., 2003b; Song et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on fetal and neonatal VWM.

claim: Disease onset <4 years of age is followed by a rapid deterioration of symptoms in VWM.
source: Disease onset <4 years of age is followed by a rapid deterioration of symptoms, while disease onset >4 years of age shows greater variability in disease course (VWM Research Group et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on disease course.

claim: There is no treatment for VWM disease.
source: There is no treatment for VWM disease, and current mouse models only partially recapitulate disease pathophysiology (Geva et al., 2010; Dooves et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of treatment for VWM.

claim: The eIF2B complex is a heteropentameric guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF2).
source: The eIF2B complex is a heteropentameric guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF2), which governs the rate of global protein synthesis and cap-dependent translation initiation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the eIF2B complex.

claim: The eIF2B complex functions to displace eIF5 from inactive GDP-bound eIF2 to allow its recruitment to the ribosome.
source: The eIF2B complex also functions to displace eIF5 from inactive GDP-bound eIF2 to allow its recruitment to the ribosome (Jennings and Pavitt, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on eIF2B function.

claim: The eIF2B complex plays a central role in the cellular integrated stress response (ISR).
source: Importantly, the eIF2B complex plays a central role in the cellular integrated stress response (ISR).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the eIF2B complex and ISR.

claim: Stress-dependent kinase activation leads to phosphorylation of eIF2, which binds eIF2B more tightly and reduces overall protein synthesis.
source: Stress-dependent kinase activation leads to phosphorylation of eIF2, which binds eIF2B more tightly and reduces overall protein synthesis (Krishnamoorthy et al., 2001; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on the ISR mechanism.

claim: In human cell lines, translation is suppressed to a greater degree after stress in VWM patients.
source: In human cell lines, it has been shown that translation is suppressed to a greater degree after stress in VWM patients (Moon and Parker, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on translation suppression in VWM.

claim: The suppression of translation lasts for a longer period of time in VWM cells.
source: This suppression of translation lasts for a longer period of time in VWM cells, and the protein responsible for de-phosphorylating eIF2 and allowing translation recovery, GADD34, was found in lower quantities.
evidence: This is an inference from the cited study (Moon and Parker, 2018).

claim: Mouse lines with knock-in/knock-out mutations in Eif2b5R132H have impaired motor function, growth deficits, delayed development of white matter, and abnormal abundance of oligodendrocytes and astrocytes.
source: Mouse lines with knock-in/knock-out mutations in Eif2b5R132H, a common allele of VWM patients, have impaired motor function, growth deficits, delayed development of white matter, and abnormal abundance of oligodendrocytes and astrocytes (Geva et al., 2010; Atzmon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on mouse models of VWM.

claim: PERK misexpression in oligodendrocytes caused hypomyelination, oligodendrocyte damage, and myelin loss in young mice.
source: PERK misexpression caused hypomyelination, oligodendrocyte damage, and myelin loss (Lin et al., 2014). However, this result was only seen in young mice, and could not be induced in mature animals.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on PERK misexpression.

claim: ISR activation has been identified in VWM patient brain autopsy samples.
source: ISR activation has been identified in VWM patient brain autopsy samples (van Kollenburg et al., 2006) and in mouse VWM models (Wong et al., 2019; Abbink et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on ISR activation in VWM.

claim: ISRIB has been shown to bind to and activate the decameric, functional eIF2B complex.
source: A small molecule inhibitor of the ISR, ISRIB, has been shown to bind to and activate the decameric, functional eIF2B complex (Sidrauski et al., 2013; Sidrauski et al., 2015; Wong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on ISRIB.

claim: eIF2B is expressed globally but VWM primarily affects the CNS.
source: eIF2B is expressed globally but VWM primarily affect the CNS, including differential effects in the CNS.
evidence: This is an observation about the paradox of VWM pathology.

claim: Oligodendrocyte numbers are decreased in affected white matter, but they are increased in other areas in VWM.
source: For example, oligodendrocyte numbers are decreased in affected white matter, but they are increased in other areas (Van Haren et al., 2004; Bugiani et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on oligodendrocyte changes in VWM.

claim: GEF activity of the eIF2B complex does not appear to correlate with VWM disease severity.
source: GEF activity of the eIF2B complex does not appear to correlate with VWM disease severity (Liu et al., 2011), suggesting that the overall protein translation is not the key component of VWM pathophysiology.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on GEF activity and disease severity.

claim: Rapid clinical deterioration and white matter loss in VWM can be provoked by a stressor, such as minor head trauma or mild illness.
source: Another unusual and poorly understood aspect of VWM is that rapid clinical deterioration and white matter loss can be provoked by a stressor, such as minor head trauma or mild illness (van der Knaap et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a clinical study on VWM.

claim: Chronic ISR activation causes cellular apoptosis.
source: This is consistent with models in which chronic ISR activation causes cellular apoptosis (Bond et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on ISR and apoptosis.

claim: There is some evidence that a de-regulated ISR is not alone sufficient to cause VWM pathology.
source: Further, there is some evidence that a de-regulated ISR is not alone sufficient to cause VWM pathology (Wisse et al., 2017), and in fact blocking the ISR worsens VWM pathology (Sekine et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on ISR and VWM pathology.

claim: During periods of hypoxia, ISR activation leads to retention of intron 12 in EIF2B5 by interfering with the exon 12 splice site in cancer cell lines.
source: Work studying cancer cell lines has shown that during periods of hypoxia, ISR activation leads to retention of intron 12 in EIF2B5 by interfering with the exon 12 splice site (Brady et al., 2017; Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on intron 12 retention in cancer cells.

claim: The retained intron 12 contains a premature stop codon, resulting in a truncated 65 kDa EIF2B5 protein.
source: This retained intron contains a premature stop codon, resulting in a truncated 65 kDa EIF2B5 protein, and rendering the eIF2B complex unable to initiate translation.
evidence: This is an inference from the cited study (Brady et al., 2017) and the mechanism of intron retention.

claim: ISR activation is mainly triggered by atf4 up-regulation in the eif2b mutants.
source: qRT-PCR analysis showed atf4, bip, and chop II expression were increased, but perk had variable expression in eif2b2 and eif2b5 homozygous mutants (Figure 8E), indicating that ISR activation is mainly triggered by atf4 up-regulation the in eif2b mutants.
evidence: This is an inference from the qRT-PCR data showing consistent atf4 upregulation.

claim: Truncated EIF2B5 was sufficient to activate the ISR.
source: qRT-PCR showed that ISR markers including atf4, chop II, bip and perk, were up-regulated (Figure 8F), indicating that truncated EIF2B5 was sufficient to activate the ISR.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data showing ISR marker upregulation after truncated EIF2B5 expression.

claim: In VWM patients, stress would activate the ISR, and would also lead to expression of truncated EIF2B5 expression; which would cause a feed-forward mechanism of further and chronic ISR activation.
source: But in VWM patients, stress would activate the ISR, and would also lead to expression of truncated EIF2B5 expression; which would cause a feed-forward mechanism of further and chronic ISR activation (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data showing truncated EIF2B5 expression and ISR activation.

claim: Chronic activation of the ISR is observed in human autopsy samples and in a mouse VWM model.
source: This chronic activation of the ISR is observed in human autopsy samples and in a mouse VWM model (van der Voorn et al., 2005; van Kollenburg et al., 2006; Wong et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on ISR activation in VWM.

claim: The truncated EIF2B5 permits formation of the eIF2B complex and a partial catalytic domain, but is missing the eIF2α interaction domain.
source: The truncated EIF2B5 permits formation of the eIF2B complex and a partial catalytic domain, but is missing the eIF2α interaction domain. This would result in impaired translation mechanism and a decrease in protein synthesis (Adomavicius et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structure of truncated EIF2B5 and a citation to a study on eIF2B structure-function.

claim: ISRIB can inhibit the ISR in mice bearing an Eif2b5R132H/R132H VWM mutation.
source: Major advances in the past several years have shown that a small molecule stabilizing the decameric eIF2B complex (ISRIB - ISR InhiBitor) can boost the GEF activity of wild-type and VWM mutant eIF2B complexes (Tsai et al., 2018; Wong et al., 2018) and can inhibit the ISR in mice bearing an Eif2b5R132H/R132H VWM mutation (Wong et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on ISRIB in VWM models.

claim: It is not clear whether ISRIB or other drugs targeting eIF2B complex stability will be sufficient to prevent stress-induced ISR chronic, feed-forward activation.
source: However, it is not clear whether ISRIB or other drugs targeting eIF2B complex stability will be sufficient to prevent stress-induced ISR chronic, feed-forward activation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the proposed feed-forward mechanism.

claim: Therapies for VWM may need a combinatorial approach incorporating eIF2B stabilization at baseline; and prevention of stress-induced truncated eIF2B5 expression.
source: Therapies for VWM may need a combinatorial approach incorporating eIF2B stabilization at baseline; and prevention of stress-induced truncated eIF2B5 expression.
evidence: This is speculation about future therapeutic approaches based on the findings.

claim: The mutations generated in zebrafish are not specifically homologous to known human VWM patient disease alleles.
source: The mutations we have generated are not specifically homologous to known human VWM patient disease alleles.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of the zebrafish mutations generated.

claim: The range of phenotypes in zebrafish mutants, from lethality in the first several weeks of life, to viability and fecundity, provide an opportunity to further study genotype-phenotype relationships in VWM.
